\label{lemma-last-one-flat}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ be a bounded above complex of flat
$\mathcal{O}$-modules with tor-amplitude in $[a, b]$.
Then $\Coker(d_{\mathcal{E}^\bullet}^{a - 1})$ is a flat
$\mathcal{O}$-module.

Finite Tor dimension means such a bounded interval exists; **locally** finite Tor dimension means each object has a cover on which a finite interval exists (the interval may vary). Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $E$ be an object of
$D(\mathcal{O})$. Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$ with $a \leq b$. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ has tor-amplitude in $[a, b]$.
\item $E$ is represented by a complex
$\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ of flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules with
$\mathcal{E}^i = 0$ for $i \not \in [a, b]$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, E∈D(O), and a≤b integers.
conclusions: E has Tor-amplitude [a,b] **if and only if** it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex E^bullet of flat O-modules vanishing outside cohomological degrees [a,b].

semantic_review_note: The criterion E has finite Tor-amplitude [a,b] iff it admits a flat representative vanishing outside [a,b] is encoded as a genuine equivalence with integer a≤b and no extra boundedness of ambient site.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bounded-below-tor-amplitude}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $E$ be an object of
$D(\mathcal{O})$. Let $a \in \mathbf{Z}$. The following
are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ has tor-amplitude in $[a, \infty]$.
\item $E$ can be represented by a K-flat complex $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$
of flat $\mathcal{O}$-modules with $\mathcal{E}^i = 0$ for
$i \not \in [a, \infty]$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, we can choose $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ such that any pullback
by a morphism of ringed sites is a K-flat complex with flat terms.
hold_reason: The pinned source asserts a true biconditional between Tor-amplitude [a,∞] and existence of a lower-bounded termwise flat K-flat representation, followed by a further choice of such representation stable under arbitrary pullbacks. The single structured logical_form 'enumerated_conjunction' loses the equivalence-specific classification needed for hypothesis/result searching, although the first prose conclusion has 'iff'.
proposed_correction: Encode a biconditional equivalence side for the two characterizations with a separate supplementary existence assertion of pullback-stable K-flat flat resolution; keep every bound and condition; independent re-review.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback}
Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
be a morphism of ringed sites.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$.
If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
then $Lf^*E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$.

For a ringed site (C,O), an object E∈D(O) has **Tor-amplitude in [a,b]** (integers a≤b) if H^i(E⊗^L_O F)=0 for every O-module F and every i outside [a,b]. Finite Tor dimension means such a bounded interval exists; **locally** finite Tor dimension means each object has a cover on which a finite interval exists (the interval may vary). An O-module F has Tor dimension ≤d when F[0] has Tor-amplitude in [−d,0] (source Definition tor-amplitude lines 12376–12394). The derived pullback Lf^* is contravariant on sites: for f:(C,O_C)→(D,O_D), it takes **objects on D to objects on C**. No flatness of f is required.

Let $(f, f^\sharp) : (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$
be a morphism of ringed sites.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$.
If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
then $Lf^*E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$.
hypotheses: f:(C,O_C)→(D,O_D) is a morphism of ringed sites.

semantic_review_note: Derived pullback along any ringed-site morphism f preserves Tor-amplitude interval [a,b] of an object E over target D, with no flatness assumption on f and correct source-target orientation.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-bounded}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}$ be a sheaf of ideals.
Let $K$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
is bounded above, then
$K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
is uniformly bounded above for all $n$.
\item If $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I})$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$,
then $K \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} \mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n$
as an object of $D(\mathcal{O}/\mathcal{I}^n)$
has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$ for all $n$.
\end{enumerate}

For a ringed site (C,O), an object E∈D(O) has **Tor-amplitude in [a,b]** (integers a≤b) if H^i(E⊗^L_O F)=0 for every O-module F and every i outside [a,b]. Finite Tor dimension means such a bounded interval exists; **locally** finite Tor dimension means each object has a cover on which a finite interval exists (the interval may vary). An O-module F has Tor dimension ≤d when F[0] has Tor-amplitude in [−d,0] (source Definition tor-amplitude lines 12376–12394). Let I⊂O be a **sheaf of ideals**; derived tensor reduction modulo I^n produces a complex in D(O/I^n). Uniformly bounded above means there exists one upper cohomological bound valid for **all positive n**. The second clause must distinguish Tor-amplitude as an O/I^n-module from Tor-amplitude over O.

conclusions: If K⊗^L_O (O/I) is bounded above, then the reductions K⊗^L_O(O/I^n) are **uniformly** bounded above for all n≥1.
If the reduction K⊗^L_O(O/I), as an object of D(O/I), has Tor-amplitude [a,b], then for every n≥1 the reduction K⊗^L_O(O/I^n), considered in D(O/I^n), has the same Tor-amplitude [a,b].

Stalkwise Tor-amplitude uses derived stalks E_p over the local stalk ring O_p. The **converse** requires the site to have **enough points** and is not asserted for arbitrary sites.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$, then for every point $p$
of the site $\mathcal{C}$ the object $E_p$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_p)$
has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$.
\item If $\mathcal{C}$ has enough points, then the converse is true.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, E∈D(O) and a≤b integers.
conclusions: If E has Tor-amplitude [a,b], then every stalk E_p has Tor-amplitude [a,b] over O_p.
Conversely, if C has enough points and every stalk E_p has Tor-amplitude [a,b], then E has Tor-amplitude [a,b].

semantic_review_note: Tor-amplitude [a,b] passes to all derived stalks at any site point, while reflection from all stalks to E requires C to have enough points; the extra hypothesis is scoped exclusively to the converse.
